headline: Approved variances for an addition at 66 Hope St and a patio roof at 512 Cottage St; cannabis business request at 92 East Ave continued.
summary: The meeting approved two dimensional variances for home projects: an addition at 66 Hope St and a roof over a patio at 512 Cottage St. Each was approved by a 5-0 vote. A use variance request to operate a retail cannabis business at 92 East Ave was continued to a later date.
decisions: Approved a dimensional variance to build an addition at 66 Hope St that does not comply with the zoning ordinance, 5-0.
Approved a dimensional variance for a 16ft by 30ft roof over a patio at 512 Cottage St, 5-0.
Continued the use variance for a retail cannabis business at 92 East Ave to a later date, to be handled by the Planning Commission.

APPEAL NO. 1:
 
Belinda L. Phillippe, Applicant and Owner of the property at 66 Hope St, further
identified as Tax Assessor's Plat 46 Lot 209, located in an “RM” Residential Multi-family Zone, is
requesting a Dimensional Variance under Section 410-44 of the Pawtucket Zoning Ordinance.  The
applicant is proposing to construct an addition to the existing structure not in compliance with the
zoning ordinance.
A formal hearing was conducted on July 27, 2026.
Mr. Ferland motioned to approve the applicant’s appeal for Dimensional Variance under Section
410-44 of the Pawtucket Zoning Ordinance, to construct an addition to the existing structure not in
compliance with the zoning ordinance; and was seconded by Ms. McLaughlin.

The appeal was approved with a 5-0 vote.
FINDINGS:
The subject property is currently occupied by an existing multi-family home.
Per Section 410-44, a minimum of (8) ft. setback is required from the side lot lines, and the proposed
addition will have a 6-foot 9.5-inch setback, a 1-foot 2.5-inch relief.
The enclosed porch is on the side of the house with structural concerns.
The existing porches will be demolished and a new porch constructed.
The relief is necessary to allow the residents to work from home by providing a functional office space.
This appeal is in conformance with the City of Pawtucket’s Comprehensive Plan as outlined in the
advisory opinion of the Department of Planning and Redevelopment.
The hardship is not the result of any prior action of the applicant, since the addition has not been
constructed yet.
It would be more than a mere inconvenience, meaning that the relief sought is minimal to a
reasonable enjoyment of the permitted use to which the property is proposed to be devoted.  This
addition will provide office space for the residents to work from home.
This Application does not propose any additional residential units and, as such, there will be no
increase in density.
The subject site and adjoining properties are zoned Residential Multifamily (RM).  The applicant
proposes to remove the existing closed-in front porches, which are in need of substantial repair.  The
applicant proposes to replace the first-floor porch with a permanent addition in the same footprint.
SPECIAL CONDITIONS:
All necessary building and other permits shall be obtained.
SEE STENOGRAPHER’S NOTES
APPEAL NO. 2: Barbara and James Winters, Applicant and Owner of the property at 512 Cottage St,
further identified as Tax Assessor's Plat 10 Lot 136, located in an “RT” Residential Two-family Zone, is
requesting a Dimensional Variance under Sections 410-44 of the Pawtucket Zoning Ordinance.  The
applicant is proposing to construct a 16ft by 30ft roof over an existing patio that is not in conformance
with the 30% lot coverage maximum. The proposed lot coverage would be 40%.
A formal hearing was conducted on July 27, 2026.
Mr. Ferland motioned to approve the applicant’s appeal for Dimensional Variance under Section
410-44 of the Pawtucket Zoning Ordinance, to construct an addition to construct a 16ft by 30ft roof
over an existing patio that is not in conformance with the 30% lot coverage maximum; and was
seconded by Mr. Miniati.

FINDINGS:
Per Section 410-44, the maximum lot coverage allowed is 30%.  The applicant proposed to increase the
lot coverage to 40%.
Page 3 of 3
August 3, 2026 - Board of Appeals Voting Meeting
The hardship is not the result of any prior action of the applicant, since the roof over the existing patio
has not been constructed yet.
It would be more than a mere inconvenience, meaning that the relief sought is minimal to a
reasonable enjoyment of the permitted use to which the property is proposed to be devoted.  A roof
with no sides will provide shade and extended use of the existing backyard patio.
This appeal is in conformance with the City of Pawtucket’s Comprehensive Plan as outlined in the
advisory opinion of the Department of Planning and Redevelopment.
The requested variance is generally consistent with the surrounding area.  The subject site and
adjoining properties are zoned Residential Two-family (RT).  The applicant is proposing to construct a
16ft by 30ft roof over an existing patio.
SPECIAL CONDITIONS:
All necessary building and other permits shall be obtained.  The patio shall not be enclosed.
SEE STENOGRAPHER’S NOTES
APPEAL NO. 3: Gary Dantzler, Applicant, and Houses for the Community LLC, Owner of the
property at 92 East Ave, further identified as Tax Assessor's Plat 53, Lot 580, located in an “RD3”
Riverfront Mixed-Use Zone, are requesting a Use Variance under Sections 410-12.7(B)
 
and 410.12(G) of
the Pawtucket Zoning Ordinance.  The applicant is proposing to operate a retail cannabis business at the
property, which is not allowed in a Riverfront Mixed-Use Zone.
This application has been continued to a later date.  It will be handled by the Planning Commission.
